subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the value of sin330° · cos120° + cos210° · sin300°.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reduce each angle
steps.margin_note: First mark. Each angle goes to its acute partner with a sign attached. Write all four reductions before multiplying anything.
steps.memory_tip: Each angle goes to its acute partner WITH a sign. Write all four reductions before multiplying.

recall.must_convey: That all four angles are reduced to acute ones with the correct signs: −1/2, −1/2, −√3/2, −√3/2.
accept: reduce each angle to an acute one with its sign, all four come out negative
sin three thirty is minus a half and cos one twenty is minus a half and so on
use allied angles to reduce all four
naalugu angles ni acute ga marchali, anni minus vasthai
each reduces to a known value with a minus

steps.why: Every one of these four angles lies outside the first quadrant, so every one picks up a sign. Getting all four right is the whole first mark.
common_mistakes: Losing a sign on one of the four.

steps.label: Substitute and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two negatives multiply to a positive in each product, so both terms are positive and they add.
steps.memory_tip: Two negatives multiply to a positive in each product, so both terms are positive and add to 1.

accept: a quarter plus three quarters is one
both products are positive and they add to one
one by four plus three by four equals one

steps.why: Both products are a negative times a negative, so both come out positive — and a quarter plus three quarters is exactly 1.
common_mistakes: Getting a negative answer by mishandling the signs.

insider_note: Reduce all four angles into the first quadrant first; every one comes out negative, so both products end up positive. 1/4 + 3/4 = 1 exactly.
